survey: A saguaro-style cactus stands upright in rolling sand under an orange diamond-pattern backdrop. The camera sits a little above the ground, looking slightly down: the sand recedes toward a horizon, and the rocks show their top faces. The main trunk is a vertical ribbed column. Its ribs run straight up and stay parallel, then curve together at the rounded top, where a pink flower sits on a small bud and is seen slightly from above. The left arm comes out from behind the trunk's left side, bends upward, and ends in a dome whose ribs meet at its tip. The right arm comes forward from the trunk's right side, overlaps the trunk's edge, and bends up the same way, so the two arms sit at different depths. All three columns stay vertical and share one viewpoint. Spines sit along the rib lines and get closer together near each column's silhouette, as they should on a curved surface. The trunk goes into the sand through a shallow hollow ring. Its bottom edge curves slightly downward toward the viewer, which matches the view from above. The rocks and pebbles in the foreground and background shrink with distance and sit flat on the sand.
